newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Gold sell-off could see Queensland miners closing.
newsitem.headline: Gold sell-off could see Queensland miners closing.

text.p: The Queensland Mining Council said continuing falls in the world gold price could see many Queensland gold miners forced to close as their operations become uneconomic.
"It's quite possible (gold) operations could close. A lot of companies must be re-assessing their position," Queensland Mining Council director of operations, Barrie Mathias told Reuters.
Gold prices slumped to a 12-year low on Thursday after news that the Reserve Bank of Australia had sold 167 metric tons of gold reserves in recent month.
At the COMEX in New York, gold for August delivery closed down US$7.10 an ounce at $325.20 after setting a new life-of-contract low at $324.00.
Mathias said any gold miner struggling to survive before the announcement by the Reserve that it had sold two-thirds of its gold reserves, would be in trouble now.

Mathias said a lot of Queensland gold mining companies had already tightened their belts and many would be now be struggling under the burden of operating costs well above the current gold price level.
Forward selling would have protected some gold miners, Mathias said.
"Forward selling helps but for how long?," he said.
Mathias said the greatest effect of a falling gold price would be felt by Western Australian companies but the comparatively fewer numbers in Queensland would also be affected.
"Everybody will be affected, not just Queensland companies," Mathias said.
